summary: @onereach/step-conversation preinstall fetches Bun runtime and executes obfuscated payload
details: package.json declares `preinstall: node setup.mjs`, which runs automatically on `npm install`. setup.mjs is obfuscator.io-style obfuscated (identifiers like `_0x488df8`, per-call parameter lookup tables) and downloads the Bun runtime binary from the oven-sh/bun release archive for the current platform, extracts it, chmods it executable, and invokes it against a bundled 727KB file `math_init.js` shipped inside the tarball. math_init.js is itself heavily obfuscated with a shuffled numeric string-array decoder (`WV8StW` shift-rotate + `n7gIxM` numeric table, single-letter symbols) and exposes no readable URLs, imports, or endpoints. The package's declared purpose is a conversation-step library; there is no purpose alignment for fetching an alternate runtime to execute an opaque, obfuscated blob at install time. The alternate-runtime choice (Bun rather than Node) evades Node-only static analysis of the payload, and the cover-story filename `math_init.js` obscures its function. This is an install-time dropper: installing the package auto-executes attacker-controlled obfuscated code on the installer's host under a freshly-fetched runtime.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
